attributes.description: Kibana events that named an object, newest first and capped at the newest 1,000 in range: reads and changes, with the object’s name, type and space. Objects that carry no saved_object fields (workflows, ML jobs, agent-builder agents and tools) are recovered from the event message, so they appear here too. Leaves out what the noise gate calls Kibana query internals: views of this audit suite’s own dashboards, searches and data view, the suite’s automated install (the API imports, exports and writes that deploy it, made with no browser session), page-load lookups, space lookups and point-in-time paging, which otherwise filled every row with the suite watching itself. It is a test of what happened, never of who or where: creating or deleting a space and everything Kibana deletes along with it (its settings, usage counters and the objects in it), and test or probe objects, stay, the suite’s own review tooling included, because they are real changes. A usage counter (Kibana’s per-object view count) has no title and a composite id, so its Object leads with the object it counts: “cloud-audit-…-02-kibana-objects (dashboard viewed counter, 2026-10-14)”. The advanced-settings object reads “Advanced settings 9.6.0”, its id being the Kibana version. A suite object a person changed in Kibana is kept, and every change, the install’s included, is in Mutations on Kibana Object Forensics. Kibana’s own page and API requests (http_request) and logins name no object and are left out too. Object is the title the object had when the event was recorded, so a renamed object shows its old title on older rows; the id in Message does not change. Message is the sentence Kibana wrote for the event. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.
